newsitem.title: USA: Portland says holders will gain from Enron.
newsitem.headline: Portland says holders will gain from Enron.

text.p: Portland General Corp said that the decision to accept fewer Enron Corp shares under the terms of its proposed merger with Enron reflected the improved chance of getting the deal through the Oregon state regulator.

The boards of Enron and Portland said on Monday that they would meet the demand of the Oregon Public Utilities Commission (OPUC) to increase savings for consumers to $141 million and as a result, Portland shareholders would receive 0.9875 Enron shares for each Portland share, not one for one.
"This is a very modest reduction in the ratio in return for increasing the likelihood that the merger will go ahead," Portland's chief executive Ken Harrison told a conference call.

"We will be able to protect (the) most value of the original transaction for shareholders. This merger represents not just the best course of action today, but the best course we could see in any reasonable timeframe," he added.
